title: Part Four, Chapter 10: The Conquests of Quicab

verses.t: And here is told of the sixth generation, which had two great lords: one was called Zacquicab and the other Cavizimah. And Zacquicab and Cavizimah did many things, and this one made the Quiché great once more, for truly he was a worker of wonders. And he was the one who divided and parcelled out the peoples, small and great, and moved them a short distance. And this was long ago, when the Cakchiquels were theirs, and those of Churla, of Rabinal, of Tzacualpa, of Coaqueb, of Zacabaha, of Zaculebab, of Tutunicapa, of Quezaltenango, of Guatemala and of Momostenango. And these abandoned Zacquicab and made war, and the peoples of Rabinal, of the Cakchiquels and of Zaculebab were defeated and scattered, and all the peoples were defeated. And the soldiers of Zacquicab went very far; and one or two branches that did not bring their tribute were subdued; he collected the tributes, and they were brought before Zacquicab and Cavizimah. And they were put into slavery and hardship, and shot with arrows, and they no longer had any power; and so they lay scattered over the earth, as the lightning stays in the stone it breaks and scatters. And he was a terror who destroyed the peoples at once. And before Colché is the sign of the town; and there is now a hill of stone almost split apart, as if with an axe, and it is there on the coast, and is called Petayub; and it is now plain to all who pass that way and see it, as a sign of the might of Quicab. And they could not kill him or defeat him, because he was valiant, and all the peoples paid him tribute. And then all the lords decided to wall the town, all the peoples having come to do it.

And then watchmen went out to the frontiers to keep guard against war, and they founded likenesses of towns on the mountains: "In case they come back against the town," they said, when all the lords held council. And they went out to place them in spots that would be like a wall and defence for them. "And this shall be our fortress and defence," said all the lords; and then they went out to place defenders against the enemies from each of the branches. And then they gave them their instructions when they went to place them in the spots of their mountains where they were to live: "Do not be afraid. If the enemies come against you again and want to kill you, come and tell us in great haste, and we shall go and kill them," said Quicab to the soldiers and captains. And then all the men of war went, the bowmen and archers; and then the fathers and grandfathers of the Quichés who are on each of the mountains were dispersed. They went to be guardians of the mountains and of the bows and arrows, and watchmen against war; and none of them was a stranger, nor did any have a different god, but they were the wall and defence of the town. And then all those of Chuila went out, those of Chulimal, of Zaquia, of Xabbaquieh, of Chitemah, Alezyocho, with those of Cabracan, Chabicac, Chihun-ahpu, with those of Zacualpa, of Xoyabab and of Zacabaha, and those of Ahziyabah, and those of Tutunicapa, those of Quezaltenango and those of the coast; they went out to keep watch against war and to guard the land. Then Quicab and Cavizimah sent them, and the Ahpop, the Ahpop-camba, and Zalel and Ahtzic-vinac; these four lords were sent and kept watch over the war of Quicab and Cavizimah, as the king of the people of Caviquib was called; and two others, one called Quema, of the people of Nihaibab, and another called Achacyboy, of the people of Ahan-Quiché. And these were the names of the lords, of those who sent them. And then the vassals went off to the mountains, to each of the hills; and the captains went and brought captives and slaves before Quicab and Cavizimah, and chiefs and leaders as well. And they made bows and arrows for war, and seized and captured, and became valiant warriors, those who had been placed in those spots; and the rewards given by the lords multiplied and increased when they came to hand over those they had seized and captured. And then all the lords and chiefs gathered in council, and decided in their council and said, "All the captains of the chinamits shall be chiefs; they shall be lords of throne and seat." This the chiefs decided when they gathered in council; and those of Tanub and Ylocab did likewise, all three clans of the Quiché together, when they named the captains and leaders of the vassals; and so it was. And they were not named here in the Quiché; the mountain where the captains of the vassals were named has its own name, and they were all sent each to his own mountain, and they gathered together. Xebalax-Xecamac was the name of the mountain where they were named and given their charge, there in Chuliman; and this was the celebration of their election and appointment, of the twenty captains of seat and house, by the lords and chiefs. And the charge was given to all the captains of the eleven great banquets, and they were called Zalel-ahan, Zalel-zaquic, Zalel-achih, Rahpop-achih, Rahtzalam-achih, Vtzam-achih. So the captains were named who entered and were celebrated on their thrones and seats as captains of their vassals, the Quichés, to watch over them and listen for them with their bows and arrows, so that they might enclose the Quiché and make a wall and fence around it. And Tanub and Ylocab did the same: they named the captains of their vassals to be on each of the mountains. And this was the beginning of the lords being settled and having their charge on each of the mountains; and so was their going out, when they went out from the lords, for they came from these chiefs.
